user_history.review_text:
I have a love/hate affair with pencil sharpeners. They’re necessary, but finding the “perfect” one is elusive – electric or manual. Which one?

That is definitely complicated.

In school, the manual ones were like Charlie Brown’s kite-eating tree. To get a new pencil sharpened, I’d have to sacrifice 1/3 to ½ of my pencil.

Electric ones could be bad. Battery operated tend to work be slightly worse than plug-in.

But, from the early 1990’s until around 2010; we had a plug-in electric sharpener that was awesome, so much so I even had one. After so long, they tend to stop working.

In/around 1997/1998 – I ended up with a Yikes manual sharpener. I LOVED that, but it got packed away. I brought it out a few years ago, and the ONLY thing wrong? The bottom suction part wouldn’t “stick”.

When I saw this, and having a better opinion of manual sharpeners, this looked like a good idea.

And, it is … to a point.

There are some striking issues:

✏️ Lack of directions. This is a more complicated sharpener to operate given a “hold this, pull this out” deal. You don’t know, because there are ZERO directions (no insert, nothing on the box) (-1 ⭐)

✏️ Lack of “suction” on the bottom. This has to be manually held down, there is nothing to ADHERE it to a surface (no nails, no glue, no suction). Definitely not ideal for a classroom with students lining up to use it (-1 ⭐)

Is it worth the current price of $9.14? With those issues? Not so much.

It does sharpen well, just not ideal for certain situations. I definitely wouldn’t get another one, and as far as recommending it – I couldn’t even mention it.
